proof:
Notation. e_i (i in Fin m) is the standard basis of R^m (EuclideanSpace.single i 1); |e_i| = 1, every v in R^m equals sum_i v_i e_i, and |v|^2 = sum_i v_i^2. hsNormSq M = sum_{i in Fin m} |M e_i|^2 and hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M). The operator norm satisfies |M v| <= ||M|| |v| for all v (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm), and if C >= 0 and |M v| <= C |v| for all v then ||M|| <= C (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound).

1. (a). Each summand |M e_i|^2 is >= 0, so the finite sum hsNormSq M is >= 0.

2. (b). By (a), hsNormSq M >= 0, so hsNorm(M)^2 = (sqrt(hsNormSq M))^2 = hsNormSq M.

3. (c). Fix i and put x := |M e_i| >= 0, y := |N e_i| >= 0 and z := |(M + N) e_i| = |M e_i + N e_i| >= 0. By the triangle inequality 0 <= z <= x + y, hence z^2 <= (x + y)^2. Moreover (x + y)^2 <= 2x^2 + 2y^2, because 2x^2 + 2y^2 - (x + y)^2 = (x - y)^2 >= 0. Thus |(M + N) e_i|^2 <= 2|M e_i|^2 + 2|N e_i|^2 for every i, and summing over i in Fin m gives hsNormSq(M + N) <= 2 hsNormSq M + 2 hsNormSq N.

4. (d). For every i, |(-M) e_i| = |-(M e_i)| = |M e_i|, so the two sums agree term by term.

5. (e). Suppose hsNormSq M = 0. A finite sum of nonnegative terms is 0 only if every term is 0 (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg), so |M e_i|^2 = 0 and hence M e_i = 0 for every i. For any v in R^m, v = sum_i v_i e_i, so by linearity M v = sum_i v_i M e_i = 0. Two continuous linear maps that agree at every vector are equal, so M = 0. (For m = 0, R^m = {0} and the same argument applies with empty sums.)

6. (f). Let v be in R^m. By linearity and the triangle inequality, |M v| = |sum_i v_i M e_i| <= sum_i |v_i| |M e_i|. By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for finite sums (Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq), (sum_i |v_i| |M e_i|)^2 <= (sum_i |v_i|^2)(sum_i |M e_i|^2) = |v|^2 hsNormSq M. Since 0 <= |M v| <= sum_i |v_i| |M e_i|, squaring gives |M v|^2 <= hsNormSq M |v|^2 = (hsNorm M |v|)^2 by (b); as |M v| >= 0 and hsNorm M |v| >= 0, it follows that |M v| <= hsNorm M |v|. Since hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M) >= 0, the operator-norm bound gives ||M|| <= hsNorm M.

7. (g). For each i, |M e_i| <= ||M|| |e_i| = ||M||, and both sides are >= 0, so |M e_i|^2 <= ||M||^2. Summing over the m indices, hsNormSq M <= m ||M||^2. The square root is monotone, so hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M) <= sqrt(m ||M||^2) = sqrt(m) sqrt(||M||^2) = sqrt(m) ||M||, using m >= 0 and ||M|| >= 0.

8. (L9). K is a subspace of the finite-dimensional space R^m, hence finite-dimensional and complete, so its orthogonal projection P_K exists, with P_K v in K and v - P_K v orthogonal to K for every v. By Pythagoras, |v|^2 = |P_K v + (v - P_K v)|^2 = |P_K v|^2 + |v - P_K v|^2 >= |P_K v|^2, so |P_K v| <= |v| (Mathlib: Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le). For v = e_i this gives |P_K e_i|^2 <= |e_i|^2 = 1, and summing over the m indices, hsNormSq(P_K) = sum_{i in Fin m} |P_K e_i|^2 <= m.

Every step is valid for all m, k >= 0: for m = 0 all sums over Fin m are empty, so hsNormSq M = hsNormSq N = hsNormSq(M + N) = hsNorm M = 0 = m, and R^0 = {0} forces M = 0 and ||M|| = 0, so every clause reduces to an (in)equality between zeros or to M = 0; for k = 0 every vector of R^k is 0, so all quantities |M e_i|, |M v|, hsNormSq M and ||M|| vanish and the inequalities hold trivially (the general argument above covers these cases as well).
key_steps: (a), (b), (d) termwise from the definition; (c) from the triangle inequality and (x + y)^2 <= 2x^2 + 2y^2 at each basis vector
(e): every |M e_i| vanishes, so M vanishes on the expansion v = sum_i v_i e_i
(f): |M v| <= sum_i |v_i||M e_i| <= |v| hsNorm M by Cauchy-Schwarz, then the operator-norm bound
(g): |M e_i| <= ||M|| gives hsNormSq M <= m ||M||^2; take square roots
(L9): |P_K e_i| <= |e_i| = 1 by Pythagoras; sum over the m basis vectors
